claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Great! Let me start with the first step. To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit, I need to know about your child or children.

**What is the age of the child (or children) you're claiming for?**

Please tell me:
- How many children do you have that you're considering Child Benefit for?
- What are their ages?

This will help me determine which eligibility rules apply to your situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I'm inquiring about my son Alex. He's 18 years old and lives with me at home.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have a son named **Alex who is 18 years old** and lives with you at home.

Since Alex is 18, he falls into the **16-19 age category**. For young people in this age group, Child Benefit eligibility depends on whether they're in **full-time education or approved training**.

Let me ask you:

**Is Alex currently in full-time education or approved training?**

For example, this could include:
- Full-time study at a school, college, or university
- An approved apprenticeship or training course
- Other qualifying training programmes

Could you let me know his current status?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in education or training at the moment. He finished school and he's just trying to figure out what he wants to do next.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. So Alex has finished school and is not currently in full-time education or training.

Let me navigate through the assessment based on this information.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Since Alex is not currently in education or training, I need to ask one more question:

**Has Alex recently left education?** Specifically, did he finish school within the last **20 weeks** (approximately 5 months)?

This is important because there's a special provision that can extend Child Benefit eligibility for a period after someone leaves education, even if they're not yet in work or training.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he left school more than 5 months ago actually. It's been a while now.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that information. Since Alex left school more than 5 months ago and is not currently in education or training, let me navigate to the final outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Now let me provide you with my eligibility assessment:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## **Your Eligibility Result: NOT ELIGIBLE** ❌

I'm sorry to inform you that **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

### **Why?**

Child Benefit for young people aged 16-19 requires them to be in **approved full-time education or training**. In Alex's case:

- He is 18 years old
- He is not currently in full-time education or approved training
- He left school more than 5 months ago, so he doesn't qualify for the 20-week extension period that applies when young people first leave education

### **What Could Change This?**

If Alex were to enter **approved full-time education or training** in the future, you could potentially claim Child Benefit again from that point onwards. The approved types include:
- Full-time education at a school, college, or university
- Apprenticeships or vocational training
- Other approved training schemes

### **Next Steps**

If you have any other questions or if Alex's circumstances change, you can contact HMRC or get more information from the UK government's Child Benefit pages. If you have other children you'd like me to check eligibility for, I'm happy to help!
